A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TreeDebater research. Their complete main texts, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including v1's subsequently removed checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original human evaluations of persuasiveness and opinion shifts, action-distribution analyses, validity checks, and reward-model accuracy.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds human-rated component ablations, additional stage-level evaluations, and participant statistics.

M1.justification: The two tree structures, strength-score recurrence, Algorithms 1–3, simulated audience, and speech-time search remain unchanged. Expanded scoring, retrieval, and prompt documentation clarifies existing components; it does not establish a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Kialo training data, the 122-debate PanelBench corpus, the same listed 13 motions, and Oxford-style debate evaluation with US participants. v2's two additional ablation motions are samples within the existing task; no distinct domain, population, or test scenario is documented.

E2.justification: Agent4Debate remains the comparator in the unchanged main evaluations. v2 Table 3 additionally compares full TreeDebater against variants without the Rehearsal Tree and without both trees in human persuasiveness evaluation. v1 compared those variants only through action distributions in Figure 2.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a head-to-head ablation using Gemini on two new motions and explicitly reports ten additional evaluations per stage in Appendix F. The original backbone models, debate durations, rating metrics, and stance-swapping design remain. Newly supplied participant and screening details do not establish changes to the original protocol.

E4.justification: v1's component ablation examines action diversity. v2 retains that analysis and adds Table 3, testing whether removing the trees reduces human-rated persuasiveness across opening, rebuttal, and closing stages. This is a focused extension on two motions, rather than a broad robustness investigation.

E5.justification: v1 reports standard deviations only. v2 adds confidence intervals and p-values for supplemental stage-level and overall comparisons, explicitly reports additional evaluations, and supplies 60.7% annotator agreement. This substantially expands statistical reporting, although the test and interval estimand remain unspecified. Standard deviations inserted into Table 2 already appeared in v1's appendix.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–2 and the validity and standard-deviation tables retain their values. New Table 3 reports opening/rebuttal/closing scores of 3.50/3.50/3.75 for full TreeDebater versus 3.00/3.00/3.50 without both trees. Table 9 adds a supplemental overall win rate of 71.73%; its incompletely specified conditions prevent treating it as an improvement over the original rates. Participant statistics and slightly revised Figure 2 action proportions are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, minimax-like interpretation, and strength-score Equations 1–2 are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs. Specifying the decay coefficient and adding a worked tree example are implementation and explanatory additions.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain tree-based preparation and planning, audience feedback, speech-time control, and stronger competitive-debate performance. v2's abstract quantifies DeepSeek gains already represented in v1 Tables 1–2, without changing the claim's scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new persuasiveness ablation as confirming the tree components' necessity and interprets annotator agreement and additional significance results as supporting evaluation reliability. Existing explanations concerning audience preferences, debate strategies, and limitations from small-scale subjective evaluation remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation documentation: decay coefficient 0.8, reward-classifier architecture and loss, weighted-category inference, human-tree serialization and retrieval settings, additional prompts, participant totals, and explicit screening questions. These are disclosures rather than demonstrated implementation changes. Conversely, it removes explicit 520/260-word budgets and checklist statements identifying A6000/CPU resources and supplemental code/data.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhao et al.'s 'Leveraging Topic Relatedness for Argument Persuasion' to computational argumentation and removes the Sentence-BERT citation associated with semantic retrieval. The broader positioning against argument-generation systems, Agent4Debate, and strategic-game agents remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the scientific outline are retained. v2 expands selected method explanations, consolidates evaluation procedures in Section 4.1, merges the two results subsections, separates the limitations heading, and removes the NeurIPS checklist. These are localized editorial and organizational revisions rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the document template, typography, headers, and captions. Figure 2 becomes horizontal stacked bars with an 'others' category; Figures 3–4 are redrawn, with Figure 4's flow illustration simplified. New ablation/statistics tables and demographic Figure 7 expand the displays, while existing appendix standard deviations are also incorporated into main Table 2.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing system easier to reconstruct and adds direct evidence connecting its tree components to human-rated persuasiveness, addressing a gap in v1's action-distribution ablation. These gains are limited by the two-motion ablation and insufficiently specified statistics in Table 9. Removing hardware and supplemental-access disclosures creates a smaller reproducibility tradeoff. Overall, the documentation and targeted evidence improve modestly while the main findings remain unchanged.
